solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beg for a retrial?

definitions.meaning: to beg is to plead or entreat earnestly
a legal challenge to a verdict asking a higher court to hear the case again

explanation.surface: Someone convicted pleads with the court for a second hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of an earnest request: one personal entreaty, one formal legal application to a higher court.

clue.text: A number in Malaga out to form a union

indicators.note: in tells us the number goes inside the reshuffled letters of the Spanish city
out here means disordered or awry, so the city's letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, one number

explanation.surface: A crowd in the Spanish resort of Malaga turn out to join together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes AALGAM from MALAGA, and 'in' puts M inside it after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: An alloy or blend formed by combining things is a mixture, a coming together, hence a union.

clue.text: Given freedom at bottom of page — nothing new to say

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed at the bottom of another comes after it

parts.note: latitude means scope or freedom of action

explanation.surface: A writer given free rein at the foot of the page finds nothing original to write.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, overused remark offers no fresh thought, so it is a saying with nothing new in it.

clue.text: Encourage a king to go on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the later one

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
the Ouse is a river in England (there are several of that name)

explanation.surface: A monarch is urged to take a boat out on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or stimulate feelings or action is to excite or spur someone on.

clue.text: Produced original work that's collected

definitions.meaning: wrote music or verse of one's own creation
calm and self-possessed, as in cool and collected

explanation.surface: An artist made new work that was gathered into a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is creating music or writing; the other is being calm, unflustered and in control of oneself.

clue.text: This oven has a ring outside for roasting

indicators.note: the word roasting has the letters of ring wrapped around the oven word, so it sits inside it

explanation.surface: An oven with a ring burner on the outside, used for roasting food.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrap R and ING around the answer and you get 'roasting', so it lies within that word. 'Ring' tempts as O, but it is the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for drying hops is a kind of oven, a crossword favourite drawn from Kent's hop industry.

clue.text: Their resting places certainly had their points

definitions.text: Their resting places certainly had their points

parts.words: Their resting places certainly had their points
parts.note: the pyramids, tombs of ancient Egyptian kings, have pointed tops; 'had their points' also means had their merits

explanation.surface: A wry remark that someone's burial places had their good features.
explanation.definitionFit: The kings of ancient Egypt were buried in pyramids, which literally come to a point.

clue.text: Go quietly, as a thief will do?

definitions.meaning: to creep or move stealthily, as in to slip away unnoticed
what a thief does is pilfer or take things

explanation.surface: A burglar creeps silently through a house.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is creeping softly; the other is the robber's trade of taking what belongs to others.

clue.text: Student's workplace has the best sort of computer

parts.note: a student works at a desk
top means the best, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: A student's study area boasts a first-rate machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer designed to sit on a table, as opposed to a laptop, is a type of personal computer.

clue.text: Aggressive female banker

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth, one of a race of warrior women; hence a strong, combative woman
crossword sense: a river, something with banks, here the great South American river

explanation.surface: A fierce woman who works in a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical warrior women give the word for a formidable woman, and the South American river is a crossword 'banker'.

clue.text: They test metal for a ship, taking years perhaps

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of the word years may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Metal inspectors spend years aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes AYERS from 'years'; 'taking' is only a joining word, and SS is the conventional abbreviation for a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaying is analysing ore or metal for purity, so those doing it are testers of precious metals.

clue.text: Bid to act as a tyrant

definitions.meaning: to bid is to order or command
to lay down the law, rule like a despot

explanation.surface: An instruction to behave like an autocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses concern giving orders: one a simple command, the other imposing one's will autocratically.

clue.text: Obtains help that was denied

parts.note: gains means obtains or acquires
aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: Someone acquires the assistance they had previously been refused.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for contradicted or disputed, as in a fact that cannot be denied.

clue.text: Radio buff rented small place in the country

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast
let means rented out, as a property

explanation.surface: An amateur radio fan rented a little cottage in rural parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny rural settlement, smaller than a village, is a little place in the countryside.

clue.text: Accelerates degrees at university

parts.note: steps are degrees, stages in a scale
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone races through their degrees while studying.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase the pace or intensity of something is to speed it up, a phrasal verb for quickening.

clue.text: She's crazy about university

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for crazy goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A woman who is wild about her college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' defines a woman's name: Maud, the girl of Tennyson's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Reduced the rent — having cheated?

definitions.meaning: sewed up a tear: rent here is a rip in fabric, not money paid for housing
colloquially, to stitch someone up is to swindle or frame them

explanation.surface: A landlord cut the rent, but only after swindling the tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like the money paid to a landlord, but it is a tear in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is repairing a tear with needle and thread; the other is British slang for tricking or framing someone.

clue.text: If you suffer this you won't be ableto keep your appointment

definitions.text: If you suffer this you won't be ableto keep your appointment

parts.words: If you suffer this you won't be ableto keep your appointment
parts.note: appointment here means a job or post, not a meeting; being sacked loses you the post

explanation.surface: A warning about something that will make you miss a scheduled meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appointment' suggests a diary engagement, but it means a position held.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sacked from a job is the formal removal from an office or post.

clue.text: Senior counsel competent enough to approach the case in stages

parts.note: the leading barrister in a case is the lead
up to means capable of, as in up to the job

explanation.surface: A senior barrister able enough to tackle the case step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare the ground for something gradually is to build towards it, approaching by degrees.

clue.text: Cliche of a hi-fi buff

parts.note: a hi-fi is a stereo sound system
a buff is a type, a kind of person, as in an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A clichéd picture of an audio enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'a stereo type': a hi-fi kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed, oversimplified image of a group is a hackneyed idea, much like a trite phrase.

clue.text: Extinguish a candle flame and pass on

definitions.meaning: to put out a candle by pinching or capping the wick

explanation.surface: Put out a candle and leave it for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass on' looks like handing something over, but it is a polite way of saying die.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally putting out a light; figuratively the slang phrase for dying.

clue.text: So this is pickled and not allowed to go to waste

definitions.text: So this is pickled and not allowed to go to waste

parts.words: So this is pickled and not allowed to go to waste
parts.note: food that is preserved by pickling is put to good purpose rather than thrown away

explanation.surface: Leftovers are preserved in vinegar so that nothing is thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put to good purpose, rather than discarded, has been employed rather than wasted.

clue.text: Excursion ending at nightfall

parts.note: an outing that is over by evening, finishing when darkness falls

explanation.surface: An outing that comes to a close as night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey there and back within a single day, a short pleasure trip rather than a holiday.

clue.text: Ozone's remarkably conducive to sleep

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters of Ozone's are reshaped

explanation.surface: Fresh seaside air is said to make you drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of 'Ozone's' supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A short light nap or doze is a brief sleep.

clue.text: Tips university to spend freely

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters of spend move about without constraint

explanation.surface: A college that hands out gratuities and splashes its cash around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' turns SPEND into PENDS. 'Tips' looks like gratuities but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something over or upside down is to tip it on its end.

clue.text: Animal badly laden

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of laden are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A beast of burden carrying too heavy a load.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African antelope, so a kind of wild beast.

clue.text: Amount to be surveyed?

parts.note: a building cost estimator in Britain is called a ... surveyor, whose job title names what they survey

explanation.surface: A query about how much is to be inspected.
explanation.walkthrough: A quantity surveyor is a British profession costing building work.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured amount or sum of something; the professional estimator's title suggests this is surveyed.

clue.text: Left in charge, but desert one's post

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the word for a charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge or payment

explanation.surface: Left in command, a sentry nonetheless abandons the position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left in charge' reads like being given responsibility, but it is L in FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away from danger is what abandoning a position amounts to, fleeing one's station.

clue.text: Jack may have a flutter, given this

definitions.text: Jack may have a flutter, given this

parts.words: Jack may have a flutter, given this
parts.note: a jack is a ship's flag, which flutters when hoisted on its pole; 'have a flutter' also means place a bet

explanation.surface: A man called Jack might place a small bet if offered this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name and 'flutter' like a British slang bet, but the jack is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall staff on which a flag is raised lets it wave in the wind.

clue.text: File I left for flophouse resident

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter I goes out of the word for a file

parts.note: a dossier is a file of documents

explanation.surface: A record shows that one person left to live in a cheap lodging house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sleeps rough or in a doss-house, a cheap hostel for the homeless.

clue.text: Swimmers who leap ahead when detailed

definitions.text: Swimmers who leap ahead when detailed

parts.words: Swimmers who leap ahead when detailed
parts.note: read detailed as de-tailed: these young pond creatures lose their tails and become frogs that jump

explanation.surface: Athletes who forge ahead once given precise instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'given specific details', but it means losing the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Frog larvae swim in ponds and, once their tails go, grow into leaping frogs.

clue.text: We draw back, reduced to tears?

indicators.note: back means the word for draw is read from end to start

parts.note: to pull is to draw, as in drawing a cart

explanation.surface: We shrink back, close to crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the synonym of draw to give LLUP; 'draw back' looks like recoiling as one phrase, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: When tears rise in the eyes they are said to brim, as emotion overcomes someone.
